Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

sampleSizeCalc 3.1.1 (Development)

Output & Reporting Enhancements

  • Comprehensive Output Display: Default print() and summary() methods now consistently output:
    1. Plain-text mathematical formula (Formula (plain text))
    2. LaTeX mathematical formula (Formula (LaTeX))
    3. Step-by-step calculation process (Calculation process), documenting hypotheses, input parameters, critical values, intermediate components, and rounding
    4. Literature references (Reference)
  • Calculation reports now respect the selected AUC variance model and allocation, retain non-default power for diagnostic CI-width planning, and show the rounding used before cohort dropout inflation.
  • Calculation Steps In S3 Object: All sample_size_result objects now carry calculation and calculation_steps fields documenting the intermediate steps.

Numerical Enhancements & Cross-Package Alignments

  • singleCorrelation: Fixed implementation to strictly match Machin et al. (2018, Chapter 19, Equations 19.5-19.8). Now supports both precision (absolute CI half-width) and epsilon (relative precision). Produces exact agreement with presize::prec_cor (e.g., r=0.5, conf.width=0.10 -> 867; r=0.5, conf.width=0.20 -> 219).
  • bioequivalence: Upgraded 2x2 crossover TOST from crude normal approximation to exact noncentral t distribution (Phillips 1990; Julious 2004 Equation 13). Added support for theta0 (expected geometric mean ratio, default 1.0) and custom equivalence bounds (margin_low, margin_high). Results match PowerTOST::sampleN.TOST bit-for-bit (e.g., CV=0.25, theta0=1.0 -> N=24, 12/sequence; theta0=0.95 -> N=28, 14/sequence).
  • diagAccuracy (test): Added method = c("asymptotic", "exact"). Setting method = "exact" executes an exact binomial search per A’Hern (2001), returning critical successes critical_successes alongside sample size (e.g., prob=0.85, p0=0.70 gives n=49, critical cutoff r=40).
  • Methodological hints and parameter role clarifications added:
    • steppedWedge: Explicit warning regarding the absence of calendar-time fixed effects in Hussey & Hughes (2007) Equation 8 and potential power loss.
    • singleArmPhaseII: Documented that ties in minimax total N are broken by minimizing Type I error alpha.
    • caseControlMatched: Clarified that psi is the discordant pair proportion (pi10 + pi01), not the discordant odds ratio.
    • cohortRate: Clarified that required subjects = person-time / follow-up duration.
    • diagLR: Clarified that sample size ensures the CI does not cross target_lr, distinct from fixed-width CI estimation.

sampleSizeCalc 3.1.0

3.1 — new designs (mrmcPower, steppedWedge, kappa, Riley prediction models)

  • predictiveModel + task=“plan” + outcome=“binary”: Riley 2020 BMJ method for prediction model development sample size (original paper obtained and implemented). Criteria B1 (outcome proportion precision), B3 (shrinkage target via Cox-Snell R2), and B2 (van Smeden MAPE, P <= 30) with the entropy-based max R2cs helper. Anchors exact: B3 P=30/R2cs=0.05/S=0.9 -> 5249 (matches pmsampsize), B1 phi=0.5/delta=0.05 -> 385, B2 MAPE=0.05/ phi=0.3/P=10 -> 461 (Fig 2 worked example).
  • predictiveModel + task=“plan” + outcome=“rate”: Riley 2020 criterion T1 for time-to-event outcomes — person-years of follow-up needed for precise cumulative incidence under an exponential model (exact binomial-CI search; anchor: rate=0.10/yr, t=10y, delta=0.05 -> 2366 person-years, exactly the paper’s Figure 1 worked example).
  • mrmc_power(): power calculation for MRMC studies (paired-patient, paired-reader) using the Obuchowski-Rockette mixed model / non-central F framework (Zhou et al. 2011 Eq 6.32, Tables 6.3-6.4). Verified against the book’s mammography worked example (power ~= 0.89 at n=50, J=8, delta=0.10).
  • steppedWedge + task=“test”: Hussey-Hughes Eq 8 WLS Wald power for full stepped wedge designs (original paper obtained and Eq 8 implemented directly; the EPT figure-read anchor discrepancy is documented — Eq 8 gives power 0.959 at RR=0.64 and the 80% crossing at RR=0.73).
  • kappa + task=“estimate”/“test”: Cohen’s kappa sample size per Cantor (1996), using the Fleiss-Cohen-Everitt variance factor Q = po(1-po)/(1-pe)^2. Anchors exact: Q(0.5,0.5,0.7) = 0.510 and the two-questionnaire test N = 214. (Table 1/2 QMAX values require the full FCE lambda1 term; estimate mode is conditional on the planning kappa.)

Breaking / API

  • New unified three-axis entry point calculate(design, task, outcome, ...). Combinations are validated against a master table; illegal combinations error with the list of legal ones. See docs/DESIGN_MATRIX.md. (sample_size_calculator() remains fully and silently compatible: all 17 legacy keywords now dispatch through the same shared code path, and golden-master tests assert identical results between both APIs.)
  • calculate() resolves arguments by exact name only. This fixes a latent partial-matching bug where design-specific arguments such as d could be silently swallowed into the design formal.

New features (Phase 5)

  • clusterRCT + task=“test” + outcome=“mean”/“proportion”: design-effect wrapper (DE = 1+(m-1)ICC) around the individually-randomised kernels, with cluster-level rounding (n_clusters per arm = ceil(nDE/m)) (Machin 2018 Ch.12; Donner & Klar 2000).
  • singleArmPhaseII: exact Simon two-stage designs (optimal = min E[N|p0], minimax = min N) via vectorised exact binomial search (Simon 1989), plus A’Hern single-stage (A’Hern 2001). Anchors verified against Machin 2018 Chapter 17: optimal (1/10, 5/29) and A’Hern 6/25, 12/35 reproduced exactly; the book’s minimax (2/15, 5/25) has exact power 0.7696 < 0.80 under the strict definition and is excluded (documented discrepancy).
  • rct + task=“noninferiority” + outcome=“proportion”: fills the legacy margin gap (nonInferiorityProportions).
  • twoOrdinal: ordered categorical two-group comparison via Whitehead’s formula N = 3(Za/2+Zb)2/((logOR)2(1-sum(p^3))) (Whitehead 1993; Machin 2018 Ch.4).
  • predictiveModel + task=“plan”: events-per-variable rule (EPV >= 10, Peduzzi 1996) with a pointer to Riley et al. (2019).
  • its + task=“test”: interrupted time series level-change power with an AR(1) effective-sample-size correction - marked EXPERIMENTAL in output hints (framework: Bernal et al. 2017; transparent approximation, not a validated source formula).
  • Deferred with documented reasons: kappa and steppedWedge (Machin Ch.20/Ch.13 formulas are OCR-garbled in the available PDF; require paper derivation before implementation).

New features (Phase 4)

  • Diagnostic non-inferiority/equivalence (margin designs):
    • diagAccuracyCompare + task=“noninferiority”/“equivalence”: two- proportion margin framework with one-sided alpha for NI and Z_{beta/2} for equivalence, plus prevalence screening conversion.
    • diagAUCCompare + task=“noninferiority”/“equivalence”: margin framework on the AUC difference with correlation r and all three variance functions (framework per Chow et al. 2017; application per Zhou 2011 Section 6.3).
  • diagAccuracyCompare + paired=TRUE via the three-axis API now uses the Connor kernel with psi = discordant-pair PROPORTION (the legacy keyword keeps the old sqrt-scale parameterization, locked by test).
  • crossover: 2x2 crossover with within-subject SD parameterization (n = 2(Za/2+Zb)^2 sigma_w^2 / delta^2; Senn 2002).
  • bioequivalence: 2x2 TOST on the log scale, 80-125% criterion (n = 2(Z_{1-a}+Z_{1-b})^2 log(1+CV2)/log(1.25)2; Schuirmann 1987; Julious 2004), with a replicate-design hint for CV > 30%.
  • diagAccuracy + dual=TRUE: dual-endpoint strategy computing sensitivity and specificity requirements each at dual_power (default 0.90 -> ~80% joint) and taking the max (Akoglu 2022 p.184).
  • Dispatcher gains a path flag (“legacy” vs “three-axis”) so upgrades can diverge cleanly from locked legacy behavior.

New features (Phase 3)

  • Observational study designs:
    • cohort + task=“test” + outcome=“proportion”: exposed vs unexposed cumulative incidence with 1:m allocation (ratio), optional dropout inflation, and RR parameter roles (Bhardwaj 2024 p.2559 anchor; exact-z value 294, paper’s rounded-z 293, ±1 documented).
    • cohort + outcome=“rate”: person-time incidence-rate comparison with unequal allocation (Machin 2018 Ch.6; IRR roles).
    • caseControlMatched: individually matched 1:1 case-control via the discordant-pairs formulation with the independence-within-pair approximation (Dupont 1988; Schlesselman 1982 p.174).
    • crosstab: cross-sectional prevalence comparison (PR/OR roles), sharing the two-proportion kernel.
  • paired + outcome=“proportion”: McNemar/Connor paired binary kernel with explicit discordant-pair proportion psi (Connor 1987; Akoglu 2022 Table 6A uncorrected anchor 155 at psi = delta = 0.05, 80% power).
  • rctSingleArm + task=“test”: single-arm vs fixed value for mean (Machin Ch.5) and proportion outcomes (Hajian-Tilaki Eq 6.8 anchor 153).
  • inflate_n() gains method = "additive" (n*(1+d), matching the arithmetic of the Bhardwaj worked examples) alongside the canonical “inflate” (n/(1-d)).
  • Result objects promote new metric fields: n_exposed, n_unexposed, person_time_exposed, person_time_unexposed, expected_events, n_pairs.

New features

  • Three estimation designs (task = “estimate”):
    • singleProportion: precision-based n = Z2*p(1-p)/d2 with absolute or relative precision and extreme-prevalence convention hints (Bhardwaj 2024 p.2558; anchor 323).
    • singleMean: n = (Z*sigma/d)^2 (Machin 2018 Ch.9).
    • singleCorrelation: Fisher-z precision n = ((1+r2)/(r*eps))2 + 3 (Machin 2018 Ch.19).
  • Diagnostic estimation upgrades (three-axis calls only; legacy keywords unchanged):
    • diagAccuracy + ci_method: “precision” (Zhou Eq 6.2) or “ci_width_power” (Zhou Eq 6.1, Flahault 2005; anchors 246/503).
    • diagAUC + var_method: “exponential” (Zhou Eq 6.4), “binormal” (Obuchowski 1994, Zhou Eq 6.5; CTC anchor 46/92), “conservative” (distribution-free, Zhou Eq 6.6; anchor 62/123); plus explicit case: control ratio parameter.
    • diagLR + lr_type/target_lr: log-LR CI method (Hajian-Tilaki 2014 Sections 6.4, Eqs 6.13/6.14) replacing the simplified Se/Sp-max formula for new-style calls.
  • New exported utility screen_required(n, prevalence, beta): total screening enrollment with an exact binomial probability guarantee of capturing n cases (Zhou 2011 Eq 6.3; anchor 451 at 350 cases, 80% prevalence, 90% guarantee).
  • Result objects gain hints (methodological warnings surfaced to the user) and n_required (single-sample estimation results).

New features (infrastructure)

  • New sample_size_result internals: new_sample_size_result(), validate_sample_size_result(), assert_sample_size_result() (internal three-piece constructor family) with canonical result fields (n_1, events, cases, subjects_to_screen, …) derived from legacy storage fields, preparing for new design modules in 3.0.
  • Internal numeric kernels z_alpha(), z_power(), inflate_n(), design_effect() shared by all future design modules (dropout inflation n/(1-d); cluster design effect 1+(m-1)*ICC).
  • as_sample_size_result() assembler so each design module can stay a plain calculation list.

Documentation

  • docs/DESIGN_MATRIX.md: full design x task x outcome combination table with formulas, sources, and the 17 legacy-keyword mappings.
  • docs/NUMERIC_ANCHORS.md: published worked examples used as numeric test anchors, including documented discrepancies (Bhardwaj 2024 dropout formula vs its own worked example).

Tests

  • Golden master suite: all 17 legacy keywords asserted identical between sample_size_calculator() and calculate() (228 assertions in the calculate suite alone).
